viewJson.usageTitle: How the app uses this data
viewJson.usage:
- Two places read this: the bell (list and number) and the “Waiting for you” list — on the Now page and in the overview of every area. Both show the kinds in this order and skip those switched off.
- The number at the bell adds up only the switched-on kinds that count in it (“Counts at the bell”).
- The overview of an area takes from the list only what belongs to that area and the areas in it; tasks, joins by link and reviews stand only on the Now page and in the bell, and “Today's appointments” only on the pages (the bell doesn't load them).
- The numbers themselves come from one query for news — from what you have access to. The setting doesn't change them, doesn't mark anything as reviewed and doesn't affect other people.
- System notifications are set separately on each device (“On this device”) — a kind switched off here may still notify there.
viewJson.title: View — notifications as JSON ("{format}", version {version})
viewJson.text:
What the bell and the “Waiting for you” list on the Now page (and in the area overview) show — which kinds and in which order. The setting belongs to the account (sealed in the browser) and works on every device. In the app: “Notifications” (bell → “Settings” or Now → “Waiting for you” → “Set up”, #/workspace/account/widok) → “Notifications as JSON”.
The layout of the Now page and of the area overview is fixed (since 2026-10-16): there are no own views, parts or display modes to set — so they are not in this format. The “On this device” settings (system notifications) are separate on each device — also outside the format.
What the import does:
- First it shows a plan (new order, what switches on, what switches off); it saves only after “Import”.
- Kinds from the document go to the top of the list, in its order; "on" switches on or off. Kinds not in the document stand behind them — in their previous order, switched on or off as before. So it is enough to give those that should be at the top.
- An unknown kind and a repeated kind — a warning, skipped. It deletes nothing; it creates no new kinds (the app knows them).
Return ONE JSON object, without comments.

Document:
{top}

Entry (an item in "alerts"):
{alert}

Kinds ("kind"), in the default order:
{kinds}

Example (office: submissions and bookings at the top, reviews off):
{sample}
viewJson.sampleLabel: Office: submissions and bookings at the top

tidyAll.title: Tidy the whole database
tidyAll.lead: Every address in the database is written the same way as in the registry — in answers to forms, in people's details and with the data controller; phone numbers as +48 600 700 800. New entries get this form by themselves, while typing. Here you tidy what was saved earlier — everywhere you have the key.

signup.title: New event
signup.says: Retreat, trip, workshop — a page, a date and a sign-up form.
signup.makes: This creates: an event area with a card, the main date, a form (first name, last name, phone, e-mail), a page with the card and the form, and a participants role. The rest you add in the area's “Event” tab.

group.title: New group
group.says: Choir, youth group, council — a place, a conversation and a link for members.
group.makes: This creates: a group area, a members role, the group's conversation and a link that opens the group.

course.title: Learning course
course.says: Vocabulary, catechism, exam preparation — reviews for learners.
course.makes: This creates: a course area, a knowledge base with a daily review, a learners role (they read), answer intake (you see progress) and a link for learners.

school.title: New school
school.says: Classes, curricula once for everyone, a register for each class.
school.makes: This creates: a school area, a teachers role, a scriptorium for curricula and lessons, and classes — each as an area in the school, with the teachers role. You set the timetable, pupils and register in each class's tab.
